clue.text: Rook in sheep's clothing?

definitions.meaning: to rook someone is to cheat or swindle them, to take them for all they have
a sheep's woolly coat, what it wears

explanation.walkthrough: 'Rook' looks like the chess piece or the bird, but here it is the verb meaning to swindle.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: to rook is to swindle someone, and the woolly coat a sheep wears is its fleece.

clue.text: Provide seafood when entertaining posh sailors

indicators.note: entertaining means holding within, as a host holds guests

parts.note: fish is food from the sea
U is the label for upper-class, posh usage
RN is the Royal Navy, the sailors

explanation.surface: Seafood is served to entertain smart naval men.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when entertaining' puts posh sailors inside the seafood, as a host takes in guests; U for upper-class is a long-standing British label.
explanation.definitionFit: To furnish is to supply or provide something.

clue.text: Elizabeth's favourite county

definitions.meaning: Robert Devereux, Earl of ..., was a favourite of Queen Elizabeth I
an English county north-east of London

explanation.walkthrough: The first sense refers to the Earl of Essex, a courtier of Elizabeth I; the second is the county on England's east coast.
explanation.definitionFit: The Earl of Essex was a royal favourite, and the county is the shire he took his title from.

clue.text: Old instrument mysteriously associated with Marie

definitions.meaning: a keyboard instrument whose hammers strike metal plates, also an organ stop
the ghost ship found deserted in 1872 is often called the Marie ...

explanation.walkthrough: The ship's real name was Mary Celeste, but Marie Celeste is the popular version of the mystery.
explanation.definitionFit: A celeste is a keyboard instrument, and the ghost ship is popularly called the Marie Celeste.

clue.text: Arab question and answer about one desert

indicators.note: about signals that the following pieces are turned round

parts.note: the Roman numeral I stands for one
to rat is to desert, as a rat leaves a sinking ship

explanation.surface: An Arab is quizzed about crossing a desert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns I + RAT round to give TARI, which follows Q and A.
explanation.definitionFit: A person from the Gulf state of Qatar is an Arab by nationality and language.

clue.text: Reform we hail for some time

indicators.note: to reform is to make over, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A call for reform is welcomed for a time.
explanation.definitionFit: Awhile means for a short period, for some time.

clue.text: Upstart making rare visit

indicators.note: making means the letters are worked up into something new

explanation.surface: A social climber pays an infrequent call.
explanation.definitionFit: An arriviste is a social climber, an upstart newly arrived in wealth or status.

clue.text: Visionary childhood?

parts.note: split into two words it describes being lost in imagination, a visionary state, while as one word it names early childhood

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the word splits in two to give the visionary sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Infancy is the earliest period of childhood, and in fancy describes dreaming.

clue.text: Bond once uniting globe — and Zane Grey novel

indicators.note: novel means new, so the letters take a new form

explanation.surface: A Bond film joins a globe-trotting Zane Grey western novel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uniting' and 'and' join the fodder pieces. Zane Grey was an American writer of westerns.
explanation.definitionFit: George Lazenby played James Bond once, in the 1969 film On Her Majesty's Secret Service.

clue.text: Vessels evenly distributed in currents

indicators.note: evenly points to the even-numbered letters, the second, fourth and so on, spread through the word

explanation.surface: Containers are scattered at regular spacing along the water's currents.
explanation.definitionFit: Urns are vessels, large vases or containers for ashes or tea.

clue.text: Claret chef ordered as medicine once

indicators.note: the letters are put into a new order, as if a chef had rearranged them

explanation.surface: A chef sends for claret as an old-fashioned remedy.
explanation.definitionFit: Leechcraft is an archaic word for the art of healing, a leech being an old name for a physician.

clue.text: Jonah's first and whale's last to join in band — they bring bad luck

indicators.note: first means take the opening letter of the word Jonah's
the letters are added to and placed among those of the band

parts.note: INXS was an Australian rock band

indicators.note: last means take the final letter of the word whale's

explanation.surface: Jonah, swallowed by the whale, joins a band of men who bring misfortune.
explanation.walkthrough: J goes in front of INXS and E sits inside it. A Jonah is himself a bringer of bad luck, which suits the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Jinxes are curses or people and things that bring misfortune.

clue.text: Apt rise is wasted by Near East

indicators.note: is being lost means those two letters are removed from the word rise

parts.note: the Levant is the old name for the eastern Mediterranean lands, the Near East

explanation.surface: A suitable rise in prices is squandered on the Near East.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is wasted' removes those two letters from rise; 'by' is a link meaning next to. 'Apt' looks like part of the surface verb phrase but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Relevant means pertinent or to the point, which is what apt means.

clue.text: Condensed thus, or the ends may be off

indicators.note: off suggests the letters are knocked out of their order and rearranged

explanation.surface: A text is condensed by cutting off its ends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'thus' links the definition to the wordplay; the anagram of OR THE ENDS also describes shortening, as cutting off ends does.
explanation.definitionFit: Condensed and shortened both describe text cut down to a smaller length.

clue.text: It's truly deep at sea, so they say

indicators.note: at sea means confused or mixed up, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: It is said to be truly deep out on the ocean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It's' links the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Reputedly means according to report, as people say.

clue.text: Spot on head of estate agent

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter, here of estate

parts.note: a spy is a secret agent

explanation.surface: An estate agent is spotted at the head of the property.
explanation.walkthrough: 'estate agent' reads as one profession but splits into two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: To espy is to catch sight of, which is to spot.

clue.text: The governor's weasel words?

definitions.meaning: the governor is old slang for one's father, so the governor's, read as 'the governor is', means dad is
in the nursery rhyme 'Pop goes the weasel', what the weasel goes is pop

explanation.walkthrough: 'weasel words' usually means evasive language; here it is what the weasel says in the rhyme.
explanation.definitionFit: Pops is an informal name for father, and the governor is British slang for one's father too.

clue.text: Notice head of pin left by a joker

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter, here of pin

parts.note: a card is a joker, a comic person

explanation.surface: A joker leaves a notice pinned up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' links the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A placard is a sign or poster displaying a notice.

clue.text: Might New York borough have young ladies crowned ceremonially?

parts.note: may and might both express possibility
Queens is one of the five boroughs of New York City

explanation.surface: Girls in a New York neighbourhood wonder whether they might be crowned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Might' looks like the noun meaning strength but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: May queens are girls crowned with flowers at May Day celebrations.

clue.text: Ducks missing Chandler's debut in Friends?

indicators.note: missing means a letter is left out of the ducks

parts.note: quackers is a jokey word for ducks, from their quacking

indicators.note: a debut is a first appearance, so take the first letter of Chandler's

explanation.surface: In the sitcom Friends, the ducks appear without Chandler's first episode.
explanation.walkthrough: Friends is the Religious Society of Friends, not the sitcom with Chandler; QUACKERS loses its C.
explanation.definitionFit: Quakers belong to the Religious Society of Friends, so Friends is their formal name.

clue.text: Moscow's refusal to screen Speed and Lolita?

indicators.note: screening means hiding behind or around, so the other piece goes inside

parts.note: nyet is Russian for no
mph, miles per hour, is a measure of speed

explanation.surface: Moscow refuses to show the films Speed and Lolita.
explanation.walkthrough: 'screen' suggests showing a film; here it means enclosing. Lolita is the girl in Nabokov's novel.
explanation.definitionFit: Nabokov's Lolita is the archetypal nymphet, a sexually precocious young girl; the question mark marks her as an example.

clue.text: Look good with a weapon

parts.note: a lance is a long spear used by mounted knights

explanation.surface: A knight looks good carrying a weapon.
explanation.definitionFit: A glance is a quick look.

clue.text: Receiver of cash in military camp or prison

indicators.note: in places the receiver of cash inside the military camp

parts.note: a base is a military station or camp
a till is the drawer or register that takes in money

explanation.surface: Cash is taken in at a military camp or a jail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'or' simply links the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The Bastille was the Paris fortress used as a prison, stormed in 1789.

clue.text: Fall reversed in American mutual funds

indicators.note: reversed means the run of letters is read backwards
in shows the letters lie within the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: American mutual funds suffer a fall that is then reversed.
explanation.walkthrough: The run NMUTUA sits in 'americAN MUTUAl' and is read backwards. Fall is the American word for the season.
explanation.definitionFit: Fall is the American name for the season between summer and winter.

clue.text: Subject of article by yours truly

parts.note: the definite article
yours truly is a jokey way of saying me, the speaker

explanation.surface: The subject of a piece of writing is the writer himself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' links the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A theme is the subject or topic of a work.

clue.text: Cat on island about to be excused

parts.note: pard is an old word for a leopard, a big cat
taken as written

indicators.note: about signals that the island's name is turned round

parts.note: Elba is the Mediterranean island of Napoleon's exile

explanation.surface: A cat on an island is about to be let off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns ELBA into ABLE; 'to be' links to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Something pardonable can be forgiven or excused.

clue.text: Genuine cheerleaders in alien environment

indicators.note: the alien forms the surroundings, the environment, of the other piece

parts.note: ET is the film alien, the Extra-Terrestrial
the leading letters of the word cheer, its first two

explanation.surface: Real cheerleaders perform in an alien setting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cheerleaders' looks like the pom-pom squad but means the leading letters of cheer.
explanation.definitionFit: Echt is a German loan word meaning authentic or genuine.

clue.text: Poet set down empty outside island resort

indicators.note: outside places those letters around the island resort
empty means the inside letters go, leaving just the first and last letters of down

parts.note: Ryde is a seaside resort on the Isle of Wight, an island off southern England

explanation.surface: A poet is set down outside an empty island resort.
explanation.walkthrough: D and N, the first and last letters of 'down', go around RYDE.
explanation.definitionFit: John Dryden was the leading English poet of the late seventeenth century.

clue.text: Look for birdbrain attacked by bird, reportedly

indicators.note: reportedly means the words are as heard spoken

parts.note: a birdbrain is an ass, a fool, and attacked by a bird is pecked

explanation.surface: A fool is set upon by a bird, or so the story goes.
explanation.walkthrough: ASS PECKED, said out loud, sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An aspect is the look or appearance of something.
